category_pages.name: Competitors & Races
category_pages.chart_note: Relay, obstacle, marathon and triathlon events the segment might substitute for a Ragnar. Bubble = US monthly search volume; grey band = the average entity in this deck.
category_pages.insight_title:
RELAYS AND TURKEY TROTS,
NOT IRONMAN
category_pages.insight:
The segment's nearest neighbours are other point-to-point team relays: Reach the Beach, Red Rock Relay, Seattle to Portland, Hood to Coast and The Speed Project all sit above the band, as do Zion Half Marathon and Wasatch Back — Ragnar's own markets. Tough Mudder and Spartan Race are positive too: the obstacle-course customer is the same customer, in a different format.

The one clear negative is Ironman. The relay participant is a team-endurance identity, not a solo-endurance one — a distinction that should shape both the competitive set and the creative ("the twelve", never "the athlete").

Turkey Trot is the surprise: a 60,500-searches-a-month mass-participation event that over-indexes strongly. It is the on-ramp — the first-timer who has run one 5K with friends is already in this audience.

category_pages.name: Running & Fitness
category_pages.chart_note: Running apps, wearables, shoe brands, gyms and training plans. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
STRAVA, PELOTON AND
BOUTIQUE GROUP FITNESS
category_pages.insight:
The strongest running signal is not a shoe — it is Strava, the social layer of running, followed by Peloton, F45, Orangetheory and Nike Run Club. This audience trains in groups, tracks it, and shares it. Obstacle and relay events (Tough Mudder, Hood to Coast, Spartan Race) follow, then ultra marathon and Altra, the trail shoe.

The mass fitness brands are below the band: Nike, Adidas, Asics, New Balance, Lululemon and Planet Fitness all under-index. So does the Apple Watch, while Fitbit and Whoop sit just above it. This is a specialist, not a mass-market athlete; endemic running inventory will out-perform generic fitness inventory.

For partnerships: Strava, Peloton, Orangetheory and Brooks are the brands whose audiences already overlap Ragnar's.

category_pages.name: Hobbies & Outdoors
category_pages.chart_note: Outdoor and indoor pursuits, from skiing to crochet. The strongest single correlation in the deck is on this chart.
category_pages.insight:
Skiing is the strongest correlation of the entire study, at nearly six times the top of the average band, with snowboarding second and paddle boarding third. Cycling, kayaking, rock climbing and hiking follow. This is the mountain-and-water outdoor identity of the Wasatch, the Cascades and the North Woods — which is exactly where the geography chart put the audience.

The under-index is just as instructive: crochet, hunting, sourdough, gardening, pickleball, board games and video games are all below the band. The audience is outdoors, in motion, and in season — winter as much as summer. Ski-season media and ski-town placements are a live channel for a spring-and-fall race calendar.

Fantasy football is the one indoor over-index: the same team-and-league instinct that makes a relay work.

category_pages.name: Cars & Vans
category_pages.chart_note: Vehicle models, rental brands and the racks that go on top. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight:
Three Subarus — Outback, Forester, Crosstrek — lead the category, with Thule and Yakima roof racks, Rivian and the Mercedes Sprinter beside them. Every pickup and Jeep is below the band: Ram 1500, F-150, Silverado, Wrangler, Bronco, Tacoma. The audience drives the all-wheel-drive wagon with the rack, not the truck.

One honest correction to our August working paper: at the entity level, "15 passenger van rental" under-indexes. The population that searches for it — church groups, large families — does not look like Ragnar's, even though every Ragnar team rents one. The van is the format and the creative centre of the race; it is not the targeting signal. The targeting signal is the Subaru, the rack and the Sprinter.

Minivans (Sienna, Odyssey, Pacifica, Carnival) are neutral to negative.

category_pages.name: Travel & Lodging
category_pages.chart_note: Destinations, hotel brands, airlines and booking sites. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
RACE TOWNS, NATIONAL PARKS
AND A HYATT
category_pages.insight:
The destinations lead: Zion National Park, Moab, St George, Cape Cod, Lake Tahoe, Bend — Ragnar's own race markets and their neighbours — with "road trip" and "national parks" beside them. The audience travels to run, and drives to get there.

Lodging is the second correction to the August paper. Hyatt and Marriott over-index; Hampton Inn, Super 8, Holiday Inn and Priceline under-index, and Booking.com is the weakest booking site. This is a mid-to-upper hotel traveller, not the budget-motel guest the anchor-level read suggested — with camping neutral rather than dominant. Expedia and Kayak are the booking sites that over-index.

Among airlines, Frontier and Delta sit slightly above the band; United and Alaska below it. Yellowstone under-indexes — a different tourist.

category_pages.name: Gear & Retail
category_pages.chart_note: Specialty running and outdoor retailers, gear brands and mass-market stores. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
SPECIALTY RUNNING RETAIL
OVER THE MASS MARKET
category_pages.insight:
Road Runner Sports is the top retailer, followed by Backcountry, Big 5, Dick's, REI and Scheels — the specialty running and sporting-goods channel. Trader Joe's and Nordstrom over-index alongside them; IKEA and Target sit above the band.

The mass-discount channel is the mirror image: Walmart, Amazon, Shein, Etsy, Lowe's and Kroger all under-index. Among gear brands, Hydro Flask is positive and Yeti negative — a small but telling split (Yeti's audience skews toward hunting and trucks, both negative elsewhere in this deck).

Co-op and partnership inventory should follow the retailers on the top line; the team-gear purchase — twelve of everything — runs through Road Runner Sports, REI and Scheels, not through Amazon.

category_pages.name: Sports
category_pages.chart_note: Leagues, events and teams — national and the segment's home markets. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight:
The leagues that over-index are the endurance and global ones: triathlon, the Tour de France, X Games, MLS, March Madness, the World Cup, the Olympics and Formula 1. The NFL is neutral, the NBA slightly negative, and the marquee franchises — Cowboys, Chiefs, Broncos, Lakers, Warriors — sit below the band. College football under-indexes.

The teams that do rise are the home markets: Utah Jazz, BYU, Real Salt Lake, the Utes, the Minnesota Twins and Vikings, the Colorado Rockies, the Arizona Cardinals. Sports sponsorship for this audience is regional, and it is the endurance calendar — a Tour de France or Olympic package reaches them; an NFL package mostly does not.

Ironman is negative again, as it was on the competitors chart.

category_pages.name: Food & Drink
category_pages.chart_note: Endurance nutrition, fast-casual and sit-down chains, beverages. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
ELECTROLYTES, FAST-CASUAL
AND THE UTAH CHAINS
category_pages.insight:
Nuun electrolyte tablets are the top food-and-drink entity by a wide margin — endurance nutrition, not sports drink: Gatorade is neutral and Body Armor is the category's weakest entity. Clif Bars and Kodiak Cakes follow, then the fast-casual set: Sweetgreen, Chipotle, Cava, Dutch Bros, Panera, In-N-Out.

Cafe Rio and Swig — Utah chains — over-index, which is the geography showing through; so, on the other side, do the Southern sit-down chains under-index: Texas Roadhouse, Waffle House, Olive Garden, Chick-fil-A. Beer and bourbon are neutral to negative; Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic "Run Wild" is above the band on a tiny volume.

Co-branding and aid-station sponsorship should look at the nutrition brands on the top line before the beverage majors.

category_pages.name: Family & Life
category_pages.chart_note: Life-stage and household signals — children, pets, home, money. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
HOMEOWNERS WITH DOGS AND
DAYCARE-AGE KIDS
category_pages.insight:
Mortgage rates is the strongest family-and-life entity, with daycare, Disneyland, dog boarding, the dog park and Chewy above the band. At the other end, pregnancy and pediatrician are the two weakest entities in the whole study, with car seat, youth soccer camps and family-vacation planning below the band.

Read together, that is a life stage rather than a demographic claim: this audience has bought the house and has a dog; its children are past the baby years and into daycare, but not yet into the travel-soccer years. It is the stage with the most discretionary weekends.

Age, income and household size were not scored in this pass, so no number is attached to that reading — but it matches what the vehicles, hotels and retailers say.

category_pages.name: Social & Media
category_pages.chart_note: Social platforms, streaming services, sports and news media. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
READS THE NEWS;
DOES NOT LIVE ON THE PLATFORMS
category_pages.insight:
The over-indexed media are national news and the outdoor press: Outside magazine, the Wall Street Journal, The Atlantic, MSNBC, NPR and CNN, with Barstool and Bleacher Report for sport. LinkedIn sits above the band.

The streaming and social platforms sit below it: YouTube, Paramount+, Disney+, Netflix, Pandora, Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok and Twitter all under-index; Instagram is neutral. Fox News and ESPN+ are negative.

This repeats our August finding at the brand level: the bare-brand "Ragnar" audience is a social-media audience, because it is the television fandom; the disambiguated relay audience is not. The audience layer does not make a case for growing social spend — Meta's own 2021 performance record has to carry that decision — and it does make a case for the outdoor and running press, and for news-adjacent inventory, that was never tested.

category_pages.name: Politics & News
category_pages.chart_note: Outlets, hosts, organisations and issues across the spectrum. Note the vertical scale: nothing here approaches the top entities of other categories.
category_pages.insight_title:
POLITICALLY ORDINARY —
DO NOT BUY POLITICAL INVENTORY
category_pages.insight:
No political entity rises into the top tier of this study. The strongest, the ACLU, correlates at a quarter of skiing; MSNBC, NPR, Politico and Axios follow at similar levels, and Fox News, Newsmax and Sean Hannity are mildly negative. There is a slight lean toward national, left-of-centre news consumption — visible in the horizontal position of the over-indexed entities on most charts in this deck — but it is a media habit, not an engagement.

This is the sharpest contrast with our TAB Bank work, where politics was the single strongest correlation in the data set. An endurance-relay audience is politically unremarkable, and the one unambiguous negative recommendation in this deck follows from it: political inventory, in either direction, will not reach these people efficiently, and it carries brand risk for a race that sells togetherness.

category_pages.name: Tech & Devices
category_pages.chart_note: Devices, mail, maps, fitness and payment apps, carriers. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
APPLE, GOOGLE MAPS AND
THE FITNESS APPS
category_pages.insight:
The over-indexed technology is the trailhead stack: Google Maps, MyFitnessPal, AllTrails, Komoot, Noom and Headspace, with iPad above the band and T-Mobile ahead of Verizon and AT&T. Windows 11 over-indexes as well — a desktop at work.

Below the band are the peer-payment apps — Cash App, PayPal, Zelle — Yahoo Mail, Android, Starlink and AT&T. The profile is the inverse of our TAB Bank ABL customer (Android, Hotmail, Bing, desktop-first): this is the iPhone user who navigates, tracks and meditates on the phone and pays with a card.

For media: mobile-first, app-led, and reachable inside the fitness and navigation apps themselves.

category_pages.name: Movies & TV
category_pages.chart_note: Films and series, prestige and mass. Bubble = US monthly search volume.
category_pages.insight_title:
WILD, SURVIVOR AND
THE AMAZING RACE
category_pages.insight:
The titles that over-index are the ones about endurance and competition in the outdoors: Wild (the Pacific Crest Trail memoir), Survivor, The Amazing Race, American Ninja Warrior, Unbroken and Top Gun: Maverick — with Succession and The Crown for prestige television.

The fantasy and comfort franchises under-index: Game of Thrones, Stranger Things, Dune, Friends, Barbie and Yellowstone. "Vikings" itself is neutral — the television sense of the brand word has been subtracted out, which is the definition working as intended.

For creative: the reference point is the competition-adventure format, not the superhero one. Team, terrain, clock.
